corrections.text: The headline describes WMIC as a '25-Year-Old Tool' and the Overview says it 'shipped with Windows for roughly a quarter-century.' None of the article's six cited sources (BleepingComputer, heise online, or the four Microsoft pages) states WMIC's original release date or age. This figure was not verified against a cited source and should be treated as unsourced background context rather than a confirmed fact.

The article states, 'According to heise online, new builds in the Beta and Experimental Insider channels for Windows 11 26H2 and 26H1 carry the same removal.' Heise's article discusses the WMIC removal in connection with the Release Preview channel (Windows 11 24H2/25H2), and separately describes new Beta/Experimental-channel builds for Windows 11 26H2 and 26H1 only in terms of File Explorer context-menu changes, without explicitly stating that WMIC was also removed from those specific builds.
